title: stele.yaml
description:
The stele manifest: the proto modules this repository owns, the ones it takes from elsewhere, and the code it generates from them.

This schema is not a second description of the format. A test in this repository runs one corpus of example manifests through both this schema and the real parser and fails on any disagreement, so what you read here is what the tool enforces — with the documented exceptions marked "the parser also checks" below, which are rules JSON Schema cannot express.

version.description: Version of the manifest format. Only 1 exists.

modules.description:
The proto modules owned by this repository. Each path is an import root: imports are resolved relative to it.

A manifest is not required to declare one. A repository that owns no protos declares none, and every generate input names a dependency instead.

deps.description:
Proto modules taken from other repositories.

The parser also checks: no two entries may share a name.

generate.description:
The code generation targets.

The parser also checks: no two targets may share a name.

module.title: module
module.description: A proto module owned by this repository.

path.description: Directory of the module, relative to the manifest. It is the import root: a file under it is imported by its path relative to this directory.

dep.title: dependency
dep.description: A proto module taken from another repository.

name.description: Identifies the dependency inside this manifest. A generate input refers to it by this name.

ref.description: The commit SHA to pin to or, for runs that update the lock, a branch or a tag to resolve.

module.description: The module of the producer to take, relative to its repository root. Empty takes the producer's default module.

paths.description: Narrows what is taken, in coordinates relative to the root of the producer's module. Accepts a single string or a list of strings. Absent takes the whole module.

address.title: git address
address.description:
Where a dependency comes from, in one of three forms:

  https://git.example.com/acme/example.git
  ssh://git@git.example.com/acme/group/example.git
  gh:acme/example            (a shorthand)

The shorthand prefixes are configurable. Two are built in — gh: expands to github.com and glab: to gitlab.com, both over HTTPS — and a caller that configures prefixes replaces those defaults entirely, so a manifest may legitimately use a prefix this schema does not know. The transport is part of the host configuration, not of the shorthand, so the same manifest works from a workstation that clones over SSH and from CI that clones over HTTPS.

There is no git:// form on purpose: it is neither encrypted nor authenticated, and major hosts have disabled it.

The parser also checks: each segment of the repository path must be a real path element, so "." and ".." are refused.

target.title: generate target
target.description: One code generation target: what to generate from, and what to run over it.

name.description: Identifies the target on the command line.

inputs.description: The files to generate from. At least one: a target with no inputs generates from nothing.

plugins.description: The code generators to run over those files. At least one: a target with no plugins produces nothing.

managed.description: Asks for managed-mode file options to be synthesised into the descriptors handed to the plugins. Absent means absent: no options are synthesised at all.

override.description:
The file options to synthesise. At least one — a managed block that overrides nothing reads as if it configured something.

At most one, too, and only because exactly one file option is currently permitted: the parser refuses the same option twice, and with one permitted spelling a second entry can only be a repeat.

input.title: input
input.description:
Selects the files one generation request is built from. It names either a local module of this repository or a declared dependency, and exactly one of the two.

The dependency form is not a corner case: a repository that owns no protos generates every line it has from somebody else's. A dependency input takes the module the deps entry already named and does not narrow it further; narrowing within that module is what paths is for.

The parser also checks: module must be a path declared in modules, and dep a name declared in deps.

module.description: The path of a module declared in modules. Mutually exclusive with dep.

dep.description: The name of a dependency declared in deps. Mutually exclusive with module.

paths.description: Narrows the selection, in coordinates relative to the root of the referenced module — this repository's module for module, the producer's module named by the deps entry for dep. Accepts a single string or a list of strings.

oneOf.title: an input from a module of this repository
an input from a declared dependency

plugin.title: plugin
plugin.description:
One code generator invocation.

Where the binary comes from is declared, and there are four ways to declare it, ordered by how much of the answer the manifest gives:

  1. module + version — the tool installs that exact version into its own cache with the Go toolchain and verifies the installed binary's own build metadata against it. Only a Go program can be had this way.
  2. url + sha256 — the tool downloads the binary, or an archive holding it named by archive_path, into its own cache and verifies the digest before anything is unpacked or run. This is what makes a plugin that is not a Go program genuinely pinnable.
  3. path — an explicit path to a binary, relative to this manifest. It says where the binary is and nothing about which build it is: no version is pinned and none is claimed.
  4. none of the above — the name is looked up on PATH, as it always was. The tool did not choose that binary and does not pretend it did.

Exactly one may be declared. Two would be two answers to a question with one answer.

Half a declaration is refused, and the halves are different mistakes. A version without a module asks for a version of nothing while the tool silently runs whatever PATH holds. A module without a version asks the tool to choose, and any choice it made would be one the manifest does not record. A url without a sha256 is an address, not a pin: whatever the server serves would be run.

The parser also checks: an absolute path is accepted and warned about, because in a committed manifest it resolves on one machine only.

local.description: The name of, or the path to, an executable plugin binary. It stays the plugin's name whichever tier is declared: it is what the report and the errors call it.

module.description: The Go module path of the command that provides the plugin, as `go install` takes it.

version.description:
The version of module to install. It must be exact — a version `go install` resolves to one build, written out in full, such as v1.36.12. Anything the module system would resolve at run time (latest, upgrade, patch, a branch name, a bare query) puts the manifest back in the business of generating different bytes on different days.

The pattern here checks the shape the parser checks: a leading v, a digit, and at least two dots. It does not check that the version exists, which only `go install` can say.

url.description: Where a published plugin binary, or an archive holding one, is downloaded from. Meaningless without sha256: an address says where the bytes came from, not which bytes they were.

sha256.description: The digest the download must have, as 64 hex characters. It is checked against the bytes as downloaded, before they are unpacked, made executable, run, or admitted to the cache.

archive_path.description:
The member to take when the download is an archive, in the archive's own coordinates. Required when the url names a .tar.gz, .tgz or .zip, and refused otherwise: an archive is not a program, and guessing which of its files is one is a guess the digest cannot protect anyone from.

The parser also checks this pairing, which JSON Schema cannot: whether a url names an archive is a fact about the address, not about which fields are present.

path.description: An explicit path to a binary, interpreted relative to the directory of this manifest — not to the directory the tool was invoked from, which would mean a different binary depending on where it was run.

out.description: The directory the plugin writes to, relative to the manifest.

opt.description: The plugin options, passed through as given. Accepts a single string or a list of strings.

oneOf.title: a plugin the tool installs, at an exact version
a plugin the tool downloads, pinned to a digest
a plugin at a path in this repository

file_option.description: The option to synthesise. The list is short on purpose: an option accepted here but not applied would be a promise the generated bytes do not keep.

path.description: Limits the override to the files under it, in the coordinates an import statement uses. Omitted applies it to every file.

stringList.description: A single string or a list of strings. Both forms occur in hand-written manifests, and refusing the scalar would be a gratuitous incompatibility.
